info.name: Brainixa Platform API
info.description:
The Brainixa platform API: the admin dashboard, the teacher dashboard, the student web dashboard and mobile app, the parent screens, and the public landing page all talk to it.

## How this document is organised

Every request sits in a folder path of the form **`<Who calls it> / <Feature> / <Part of the feature>`**:

| First level | Who calls it | Token |
|---|---|---|
| **Admin** | the admin dashboard | `{{admin_token}}` |
| **Teacher** | the teacher dashboard | `{{teacher_token}}` |
| **User** | the student - the web dashboard AND the mobile app (they share every endpoint; the folder's own description lists what matters on a phone) | `{{student_token}}` |
| **Parent** | the parent screens | `{{parent_token}}` |
| **Landing** | the public website | none |
| **Shared** | more than one client: public config and pricing, uploads, the payment gateway's callback | varies |

The second level groups related requests (Content, Store, Sales & Payments, Live Classes...), and the third level splits a feature into its parts when it has several (Live Classes / Zoom, Live Classes / Consultations...). Every folder carries a description of what it is for.

**Each request appears once.** Where the server accepts the same request under a second path or method (an alias kept for older clients), the request lists those spellings under *"The same request is also accepted at"* instead of appearing twice.

## Reading one request

Every request's description starts with the same three parts:

1. **Last changed in** - the most recent update that touched it, and which token it needs.
2. **What changed, update by update** - one line per update that changed it, oldest first. This is where the update numbers live now; they are no longer part of the folder names.
3. The full explanation: fields, rules, edge cases and examples.

The machine-readable `x-last-update` field carries the same "last changed" value on every operation.

## Using it in Postman

1. Import `brainixa_api_postman_collection.json` (this document as a collection, with the folders nested) and `brainixa_postman_environment.json`, then pick **Brainixa - Live** as the environment.
2. Fill in the passwords in the environment - they are empty in the file on purpose.
3. Send the sign-in request of the role you are testing (`<Role> / Account / Sign-in...`). It saves the token into the environment by itself, and every request of that role works after it.

Importing this OpenAPI file straight into Postman also works, but Postman then makes one flat folder per tag instead of the tree. After changing this file, rebuild the collection with `python tools/api_docs/build_postman_collection.py`.

## Rules that apply everywhere

- **Base URL:** `https://camp-coding.online/brain-ixa`. Every path below is relative to it.
- **A failure arrives as HTTP 200.** Business-logic errors come back with `status: "error"` and a `message`. Branch on `status`, never on the HTTP code.
- **A third outcome:** `severity: "warning"` means the write SUCCEEDED but could not do everything asked (homework saved for students one of whom has no subscription, say). Treating it as a failure hides a change that did happen.
- **Tokens are per role.** An admin token on a teacher route is refused; only *Shared / Uploads* takes a token of any role.
- **Prices:** an empty price (`null`) means *no price - not for sale yet*, which is different from `0` (free). Student and public endpoints keep `price` numeric and add `is_priced: false` for an unpriced item; admin and teacher endpoints return `null`.
- **Pagination:** most list endpoints take `page` and `limit` and answer with the rows plus `total_count`.

## What this document covers

Every endpoint that was added or changed since the base version the platform was built from (the Najeh codebase). An endpoint untouched since then is not described here yet.

## Update history

| Update | What it brought |
|---|---|
| update-1 | Subscription codes for courses, subjects and teachers; student and parent onboarding from a code; spreadsheet exports; notification inboxes for students and parents. |
| update-2 | Courses and packages as one thing with a `kind`; the admin's notification inbox; package previews and the join lock on today's sessions. |
| update-3 | Live-class attendance and the teacher wallet: check-in, absence and lateness requests, fines, appeals, the HR pay policy. |
| update-4 | Offline payments, country pricing, discount codes, dated package appointments, device-limited sign-in, referral points, the Sales page, admin search. |
| update-5 | The EasyKash card payment gateway, the question bank, course categories without a required code. |
| update-6 | The consultation and package-session cycle: meeting links, start and end, admin approval of a booking. |
| update-7 | Zoom inside the platform for all three kinds of meeting, manual sales, the chat contact directory, hero slides, and the books library turned into a store. |
| update-8 | Fix: the student's general exams list leaked unit exams. |
| update-9 | The landing page's promo sections moved into the site settings. |
| update-10 | Consultation slots from a list of dates, with an optional hourly price. |
| update-11 | Attendance reports and class ratings. |
| update-12 | Homework aimed at particular students. |
| update-13 | The Report Center: sales, attendance, payroll and ratings reports, downloadable as .xlsx. |
| update-14 | Store products and product categories of their own, and product files of any type. |
| update-15 | Moving the base currency safely; prices decided by the country a request comes from. |
| update-16 | The general file upload requires a token. |
| update-17 | Removing a purchase request that has already been decided (admin and teacher). |
| update-18 | An empty price means "no price", not free, on courses, packages, books and products. |
| update-19 | The landing page's course list says which courses have no price (`is_priced`). |
| update-20 | `subscribed=0` on the course list: what a student does not have yet, in one paged list (the app's "جديد المنصة"). Admin chat deletes a message for real instead of leaving an empty row. |
| update-21 | The landing page's courses and packages are priced for the visitor's country, like the books already were. |
| update-22 | The admin dashboard counts the store: `statistics.store` (products plus books sold on their own). |

### The longer notes some updates came with

`update-6` ports the consultation and package-session cycle from the Najeh codebase, WITHOUT its platform-owner idea: Brainixa has no owner who gives sessions without being a teacher, so every slot here belongs to a real teacher and there is no teacher_id = 0 anywhere. It adds a meeting link to consultations, start and end as a stored state for both consultations and package sessions, an admin way to approve or refuse a booking, and scopes a student's calendar to the packages they actually hold. Migrations 107 to 109.

`update-7` is the live-class batch and the loose ends around it: Zoom played inside the platform for all three kinds of live meeting (the weekly class sessions, the dated package appointments and the 1:1 consultations), a manual-sales sheet for admin and teacher, a chat contact directory read from the real tables instead of Firebase's stale copy, and hero slides as a table of their own.

update-7 also turns the books library into a STORE. No products table was added: `course_books.file_type` carries `physical` for an item with no file, so every existing book endpoint sells one unchanged. Clients branch on that field rather than assuming a file exists.

`update-8` (FIX): GET /student/exams leaked unit-scoped exams into the general listing whenever the request carried no `course_id` at all - the documented "whole-course exams only by default" rule was only ever enforced when `course_id` was explicitly passed. A student's general exams tab (no filters) could show a unit exam mixed in with the whole-course/standalone ones. The same default - `unit_id IS NULL` unless `include_unit_exams`/`with_unit_exams` says otherwise - now applies regardless of whether `course_id` is present. No response shape change, no new field; strictly fewer rows come back from the general (no-filter) call than before. A unit's own exams remain fully visible from inside that unit's content (GET /student/courses .../units, unaffected - that endpoint always filtered by `unit_id` directly).

`update-13` is the Report Center (مركز التقارير): the four reports an owner asked to be pulled automatically rather than compiled by hand - sales, live-class attendance for both students and teachers, payroll with its deductions, and the after-class ratings - each over a `date_from`/`date_to` range and each downloadable as .xlsx. No migration: every figure already existed in rows the platform writes, and each report delegates to the module that already owns its numbers, so none of them can drift from the Sales screen, the attendance report or the ratings summary. Payroll is the one report with queries of its own, because the wallet had a ledger and a balance but never a per-period payslip; it is gated on `manage_wallets` rather than `manage_reports`.

`update-14` gives the store products of its own. Until now everything it sold was a `course_books` row with no file attached, which works for a printed book and for nothing else - a school bag has no subject, no course and no unit, and the only category on that table says whether a PDF is a summary or a past paper. `products` and `product_categories` are new tables, deliberately separate from books and from course categories, and `GET /store` is the one place the two are shown side by side, each entry carrying `item_type` because an id is unique only within its own type. Nothing existing changed: no column was added to `course_books` and `GET /books` lists them exactly as before. Migration 127. Buying a product is NOT part of this batch - the catalogue is.

`update-14` also lets a product carry a file of any type (migration 128). `upload_any_file()` inverts the usual allow-list and refuses only what a web server might execute, checking every segment of the name so a double extension does not slip past; `uploads/.htaccess` already disables execution in that directory, so the deny-list is the first lock rather than the only one. `file_is_public` decides whether the shop front is given the path at all, and defaults to withholding it.

**Last changed in:** update-4  |  **Auth:** no token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **base version (inherited from Najeh)** - Part of the base version.
- **update-4** - CHANGED: Admin sign-in, now rate limited

---

update-4 (CHANGED): subject to the login limit when `login_lockout_enabled` is on (migration 074).

After `max_login_attempts` consecutive failures this returns `error_code: login_locked` with `retry_after_minutes`, and the CORRECT password is refused too until the lock expires - that is the point of it.

Counted per (email + IP + role), not per email. Per-email counting would let anyone who knows an address lock its owner out; tying the count to the source IP means an attacker only ever locks out themselves. A wrong EMAIL counts as well, or spraying one password across a list of addresses would cost nothing.

`locked_until` is stored in UTC and expires by itself, so no setting can lock someone out permanently. An admin can release every lock at once with POST /admin/login-attempts/clear. Ships OFF.

update-4 (NEW). Deletes every active lockout created by the login limit.

A lockout already expires on its own, so this is a shortcut rather than a rescue - but when the limit was set to something too low, waiting it out is not much comfort. It exists so that correcting the setting never means opening phpMyAdmin.

No body. Releases every temporary sign-in lockout at once and answers with `data.cleared`, the number released. Requires the `manage_settings` permission.

item.name: Can this admin open the chat?

request.description:
**Last changed in:** update-4  |  **Auth:** admin token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-4** - NEW: May this admin open the chat?

---

A permission probe, nothing more. The body is always `{status: 'success', message: 'ok'}` - the answer is the status code, 200 or 403.

Chat is not a PHP/MySQL feature: the dashboard talks to Firebase directly, so no backend route ever mediated who could open it. That is the actual reason chat had no permission checkbox - a permission in this codebase is only real because a route enforces it, and no route existed to attach one to. The chat page calls this before it opens a single Firebase connection, and a 403 keeps the chat UI from mounting.

Gated on `manage_chat`.

KNOWN LIMIT, stated plainly: Firebase's own security rules are not scoped per permission, so an admin who already holds valid Firebase credentials and drives the SDK by hand (browser console, hand-crafted request) is not stopped at the data layer - only the dashboard path is. That is weaker than every other permission here, which the database enforces per request. Closing it properly means Firebase custom claims plus matching rules.

request.description:
**Last changed in:** update-22  |  **Auth:** admin token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **base version (inherited from Najeh)** - Part of the base version.
- **update-4** - EXPANDED: Dashboard statistics - counts, sales, per-course sales, yearly charts and recent activity
- **update-5** - Sales now include manual and WhatsApp sales, a cancelled manual sale is excluded, and packages are counted apart from courses
- **update-22** - `data.statistics.store` is new: `total` and `active` count what the store sells (its products plus the books sold on their own - no course, no unit), with `books` and `products` beside them. Feeds the home page's store tile.

---

Everything the admin dashboard home page needs, in one call.

update-4 additions (previously this endpoint returned only the `statistics` counts):
- `statistics.courses` - course count, alongside the existing entity counts.
- `sales` - total / today / this month / this year revenue, plus a per-channel breakdown.
- `top_courses` - sales and revenue per course, best seller first.
- `charts.sales_by_month` and `charts.students_by_month` - always exactly 12 entries (January to December), including months with no data, so a chart can be rendered without filling gaps client-side.
- `recent_activity` - newest platform events, each with a `link` to the page that handles it.

No database change was needed for any of this: every figure is derived from tables that already exist.

=== update-5 ===

`sales` gains a third source, `manual_subscriptions`: a sale closed over WhatsApp or in cash used to be recorded as a subscription with no price, so it appeared in no revenue figure at all. It is now priced (migration 099) and counted.

A manual sale that was later cancelled no longer counts - `cancelled_at IS NULL` was missing, so cancelling a sale left its money in the total.

`statistics` separates `kind = 'package'` from ordinary courses; the course count used to swallow the packages.

query.description: Per-group result limit.

request.description:
**Last changed in:** update-4  |  **Auth:** admin token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-4** - NEW: Search across the whole admin dashboard

---

Query: `q` (required, at least 2 characters), `limit` (results per group, optional). Returns results grouped by type across students, teachers, parents, courses, packages, books, subjects, grades and exams; each item carries `id`, `title`, `subtitle`, `image`, `is_active` and `link` - the dashboard path that opens it.

The route itself requires only an admin session; each GROUP inside is gated on the permission of the screen it links to, so results never expose more than this admin could already reach by opening those pages themselves. Courses and packages share one table (split on `kind`) and never overlap between the two groups. `%` and `_` in `q` are escaped before reaching LIKE.

**Last changed in:** update-4  |  **Auth:** admin token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-4** - NEW: Raise or clear one student's device ceiling

---

Sets `students.max_devices`. Send `null` to clear the override and put the student back on the platform default, which is the right answer more often than baking a number onto the student forever.

The platform default itself lives in `site_settings.max_devices_per_student` and is edited through POST /admin/site-settings.

request.description:
**Last changed in:** update-4  |  **Auth:** admin token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-4** - NEW: Devices a student is signed in from

---

Everything support needs when a student says they cannot log in: which devices are holding the slots, their last IP and last-seen time, and what ceiling actually applies to this student.

Revoked devices stay in the list with `is_active: 0` rather than disappearing - 'this is the fourth reset on this account' is exactly what someone wants to know about a shared password.

`effective_limit` is the number in force: the student's own `max_devices` when set, otherwise the platform default. `enforcement_enabled` false means devices are still recorded but nobody is blocked.

**What changed, update by update:**

---

Revokes every device at once - the button support presses. The student can sign in again from whichever device they are actually holding, and any session still open elsewhere is ended on its next request rather than when its token happens to expire.

Rows are kept as history, not deleted.

**Last changed in:** update-4  |  **Auth:** admin token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-4** - NEW: Revoke one device

Frees a single slot instead of all of them - for when a student lost one phone and still wants the other signed in. POST is accepted at the same path for clients that cannot send a DELETE body.

item.name: Sign a student out of every session

request.description:
**Last changed in:** update-4  |  **Auth:** admin token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-4** - NEW: Sign a student out of every session

---

Ends every session the student has open, everywhere, immediately.

DIFFERENT FROM RESETTING DEVICES, and both are worth having:
- POST /admin/students/devices/reset frees the SLOTS, so a NEW device can sign in.
- this ends every SESSION, so the SAME device simply has to sign in again.

The second is what you want when a phone goes missing: end the sessions without also costing the student the device slot they will want back in an hour. Send `revoke_devices: true` to do both at once.

It also reaches sessions device revocation cannot see. Rather than looking for a device id, it stamps `students.sessions_revoked_at` and every token issued before that moment is refused - so tokens minted before devices existed, or while the limit was switched off, die too.

Both the auth middleware and POST /auth/refresh enforce it, so a signed-out session cannot refresh its way back in. Clients get `error_code: session_revoked` (HTTP 401 on a normal call, 403 on refresh) and should treat it as a hard logout. A login AFTER the cutoff is unaffected.

**Last changed in:** update-7  |  **Auth:** admin token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-7** - CHANGED: create a student - email, phone and age are no longer forced

---

Documented here for the update-7 validation change; the endpoint itself predates this changelog.

update-7 (VALIDATION RELAXED): `name` and `password` are the only hard requirements. Email and the phone number are both optional now, with one guard: NOT BOTH EMPTY on the same account - `"Provide at least an email or a phone number"`. An account saved with neither would be unreachable, including to its own owner, because this role signs in by email.

Before update-7 email was NOT NULL in the schema AND hard-required by the handler, so a phone-only account could not be opened at all. An email can be added later from the edit screen.

`age` is optional too. Students sign in by phone as well as by email (`phone_key`), so a phone-only student account is fully usable.

update-4 (FIXED): `fk_courses_teacher` was created with an ON UPDATE rule and no ON DELETE one, so it fell back to RESTRICT and every attempt failed with "Cannot delete or update a parent row". Every other foreign key pointing at `teachers` already declared CASCADE or SET NULL - this one was simply missed. Migration 094 rebuilds it as ON DELETE SET NULL.

The handler no longer relies on the constraint either. Before deleting it walks the teacher's courses and, where an active co-teacher already exists in `course_teachers`, hands the course to them instead of blanking `teacher_id` - a course losing its main teacher while a co-teacher sits right there is worse than just giving it to that co-teacher. The response reports `courses_reassigned` and `courses_detached` so the admin can see what the delete moved.

Everything else cascades on its own: teacher_subjects, course_teachers and affiliates are deleted, and wallet transactions have their teacher_id set to null.

query.description: The three-letter code being moved to. Must be an ACTIVE currency.

request.description:
**Last changed in:** update-15  |  **Auth:** admin token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-15** - NEW: what changing the base currency would do

---

update-15: moving the base currency can no longer reprice the platform in silence.

`courses.price` and `course_books.price` are bare numbers. Nothing on the row says which currency they are in - the answer is whatever `base_currency` says today. So changing that setting converted nothing: a course priced at 300 EGP became a course priced at 300 SAR, roughly eight times dearer, with no edit and nothing on screen to show it had happened. Setting the currency back does not undo it either, because the figures were never changed.

A price now reaches the incoming currency one of two ways and no third:
  * it was ALREADY entered for a country that uses that currency, so it is adopted. Matching is on the currency rather than on one country, since several countries share one; where more than one exists the lowest is taken, because over-charging is the worse mistake.
  * the admin TYPED it, sent as `base_currency_prices`.

Anything still without one REFUSES THE WHOLE CHANGE. Nothing is written - not the prices and not the setting - so a refusal leaves the platform exactly as it was, and the response names the items in `base_currency_blocked.missing`.

No conversion is ever invented. An exchange rate picked by the server would put a number in front of a customer that nobody approved.

Store products are outside all of this: `products.currency` is a column on each row, so a product already carries its own currency and the base setting never spoke for it. `course_books` rows DO go through it - their price is a bare number like a course's - and the dashboard labels them "منتج" because that is what the platform sells them as.

Read-only, and the confirmation screen calls it before anything is saved.

Returns `adoptable` (items with a stored price in the target currency, each with `current_price` and `new_price`), `missing` (items with none, which must be given one), `missing_by_kind` counted as package / normal / book, and both counts. `is_change` is false when the target is already the base currency.

item.name: Create consultation slots from a list of dates

request.description:
**Last changed in:** update-10  |  **Auth:** admin token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-2** - identical behavior and validation to POST /teacher/consultations/recurring (same shared core function under the hood, so the two routes cannot drift out of sync), except the target teacher is chosen by the admin via `teacher_id` in the body instead of being taken from the caller's own auth token.
- **update-4** - accepts an optional `student_id`.
- **update-6** - accepts an optional `meeting_link`, written to every slot the run creates (migration 107).
- **update-10** - CHANGED: create consultation slots - now from a list of dates, and with an optional hourly price

---

update-10 (NEW FIELD `dates`): the days can now be an explicit list instead of a weekly pattern.

`dates` takes an array of `YYYY-MM-DD` strings - the days somebody picked on a calendar. They need not share a weekday, need not repeat, and need no end date. When it is present, `days` and `end_date` are ignored.

The old form is untouched and still works exactly as it did: leave `dates` out, send `days` (weekday names) and `end_date`, and every repeat up to that date is created. It was the only form available, and it could only describe a run that falls on the same weekday every week - which most consultation timetables do not, because a week gets skipped for a holiday and two days get added before an exam.

Both forms are held to the same window: nothing before today, nothing more than 180 days ahead, at most 200 slots in one call. A date outside it is REFUSED by name rather than quietly dropped - an admin who picks twelve dates and is given nine has no way to tell which three went missing.

update-10 (NEW FIELD `price_per_hour`): optional, and blank is not zero. An empty value means the consultation is not priced, which is what every consultation on the platform was before this; a `0` means it is deliberately free. The two are stored and served apart. A negative or non-numeric value is refused. Needs migration 124; without it the field is accepted and ignored rather than failing.

---

update-2 (Admin): identical behavior and validation to POST /teacher/consultations/recurring (same shared core function under the hood, so the two routes cannot drift out of sync), except the target teacher is chosen by the admin via `teacher_id` in the body instead of being taken from the caller's own auth token. Returns an error if teacher_id doesn't reference an existing teacher.

update-4: accepts an optional `student_id`. With it, the whole run is created already booked for that student and both sides get one summary notification; the response then also carries `booked_for_student_id` and `booked_count`. Without it, nothing changes.

update-6 (CHANGED): accepts an optional `meeting_link`, written to every slot the run creates (migration 107). Where that migration has not run the field is ignored rather than failing the call.

update-10 (NEW FIELDS on every consultation slot): `price_per_hour` (a number, or null when nobody has priced it) and `is_free` (true only when a price was set and it is zero). Reading a missing price as 0 would show every slot created before update-10 as a giveaway, which is why the two are separate fields.

---

update-3 (NEW, Section 10). The single decision point for both roles.

WHAT APPROVAL ACTUALLY BUYS THE REQUESTER: it does NOT write an attendance row by itself. It records the approval, and the later automatic machinery consults it:
- an approved `absence_permission` makes the no-show cron record that occurrence as absent-but-EXCUSED, with NO fine for a teacher and NO increment of the monthly unauthorized-absence counter for either role;
- an approved `late_notice` makes the check-in flow mark the late arrival as excused, so a late teacher is not fined per minute.
This is why approving retroactively, after the cron has already run for that occurrence, will not undo a fine - use POST /admin/teacher-wallets/adjust or the appeal flow for that.

Only a request still in `pending` can be decided; anything else returns `request_not_found_or_reviewed`, which also makes the endpoint safe against double-submits.

FIELD ALIASES: `decision` may also be sent as `status`, and `note` as `admin_note` - both spellings are accepted for each.

SIDE EFFECT: the requester gets a push/in-app notification naming them explicitly and stating the decision.

---

update-3 (NEW, Section 10). PARTIAL BY DESIGN: send only the fields you want to change; anything omitted keeps its current value. Sending an empty/unknown-only body is an error (`no_fields_to_update`) rather than a silent no-op.

SANITISATION: all integer fields are clamped to >= 0, all decimal fields to >= 0, and `default_pay_model` is only accepted from the enum - an invalid value is silently ignored rather than saved. The response re-reads the row from the DB, so what you get back is exactly what is now stored.

TIMING SEMANTICS (important, and matches the product spec): changes are NEVER retroactive. Fines already charged, absences already counted and earnings already credited stay as they were; the new numbers only affect sessions and requests evaluated from this moment on, because every consumer reads this row fresh at decision time.

**What changed, update by update:**

---

update-3 (NEW, Section 10). Pins one teacher to their own pay model/rate, overriding `default_pay_model` / `default_pay_rate` from the policy row. UPSERT: calling it again for the same teacher replaces the existing override rather than erroring or creating a duplicate.

The three models and how the earning is computed at check-out:
- `hourly`      -> rate_amount x (actual minutes / 60), rounded to 2 decimals. Pays for real time spent.
- `per_session` -> flat rate_amount regardless of duration.
- `per_minute`  -> rate_amount x actual minutes.
'Actual minutes' means check_out_time minus check_in_time (floored at 1 minute), NOT the scheduled length - a session that runs long pays more on the time-based models.

Takes effect on the teacher's NEXT check-out; already-credited earnings are untouched.

Validation: teacher_id must reference a real teacher (`teacher_not_found`), pay_model must be in the enum (`pay_model_required`), rate_amount must be present and >= 0 (`rate_amount_required`).

On the public side the key is resolved before it is served: each item collapses to the single string matching the request language (falling back to the other language when one side is blank), blanks are dropped, and the result is a flat array of strings. update-15: moving the base currency can no longer reprice the platform in silence.

`courses.price` and `course_books.price` are bare numbers. Nothing on the row says which currency they are in - the answer is whatever `base_currency` says today. So changing that setting converted nothing: a course priced at 300 EGP became a course priced at 300 SAR, roughly eight times dearer, with no edit and nothing on screen to show it had happened. Setting the currency back does not undo it either, because the figures were never changed.

A price now reaches the incoming currency one of two ways and no third:
  * it was ALREADY entered for a country that uses that currency, so it is adopted. Matching is on the currency rather than on one country, since several countries share one; where more than one exists the lowest is taken, because over-charging is the worse mistake.
  * the admin TYPED it, sent as `base_currency_prices`.

Anything still without one REFUSES THE WHOLE CHANGE. Nothing is written - not the prices and not the setting - so a refusal leaves the platform exactly as it was, and the response names the items in `base_currency_blocked.missing`.

No conversion is ever invented. An exchange rate picked by the server would put a number in front of a customer that nobody approved.

Store products are outside all of this: `products.currency` is a column on each row, so a product already carries its own currency and the base setting never spoke for it. `course_books` rows DO go through it - their price is a bare number like a course's - and the dashboard labels them "منتج" because that is what the platform sells them as.

Sending `base_currency` through THIS endpoint is what triggers the guard. It lives here rather than behind its own endpoint precisely because a separate endpoint is what would be stepped around by posting the key straight to this one.

`base_currency_prices` carries the typed prices: a map keyed `"course-12"` / `"book-7"`, a list of `{item_type, item_id, price}`, or either of those JSON-encoded as a string. It is consumed by the change and never stored as a setting. Zero is accepted - an item can be given away on purpose - and a negative number is not a price.

On success the response carries `base_currency_change` with `adopted_from_stored` and `adopted_from_entered`. On refusal it is `status: "error"` with `base_currency_blocked`.

update-3: two changes to this pre-existing endpoint.

1) MONTHLY CAP. Before inserting, the server counts this teacher's reschedule requests created since the 1st of the current month. If that count already reaches `teacher_max_reschedule_per_month` from the HR policy, the request is refused with `max_reschedule_requests_reached` ('تم الوصول للحد الأقصى من طلبات التأجيل المسموح بها هذا الشهر'). Note the counter is on requests SUBMITTED, not requests approved - a rejected request still consumes one slot.

2) BUGFIX - `new_start_time` / `new_end_time` are truly optional now. The code always treated them as optional (a reschedule may move only the DAY and keep the same time), but the DB columns were NOT NULL, so omitting them crashed with a raw SQL error "Column 'new_start_time' cannot be null". Migration 062 makes both columns nullable. Omitting them now correctly means 'keep the original time'.

3) NOTIFICATION. All admins are now notified on creation, and the message NAMES the teacher (previously such messages were anonymous, which made the admin's notification log unreadable).

item.name: Start a live session (also my check-in)

request.description:
**Last changed in:** update-3  |  **Auth:** teacher token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-3** - CHANGED: Start a live session - now also the teacher's attendance check-in, and blocked earlier than 5 minutes before the start time

---

update-3: this pre-existing endpoint gained TWO behaviors. It is documented here for the first time because both are breaking-ish for clients.

1) NEW HARD TIME GATE. The call is REJECTED with `session_start_too_early` if it arrives more than 5 minutes before the session's scheduled `start_time`. In other words the allowed window opens at start_time minus 5 minutes and never closes (starting late is permitted - and is exactly what produces a 'late' record). The 5 minutes is a fixed constant, NOT the configurable `teacher_grace_minutes` (which governs the opposite side: how late is still 'present').
CLIENT ACTION: the teacher app must surface this message as an alert and keep the Start button disabled until the window opens. And because this error is returned with HTTP 200 and `status: 'error'` in the body, any client that shows a success toast purely on a 2xx will show the error text inside a green toast - branch on the body's `status`.

2) IT IS NOW THE TEACHER'S CHECK-IN. On the FIRST successful call for a given date the server records `teacher_session_attendance` for that occurrence: lateness = now minus start_time in minutes (floored at 0); status = `present` while within `teacher_grace_minutes`, `late` beyond it. If the teacher is `late`, has NO approved late_notice for that occurrence, and `teacher_late_fine_per_minute` > 0, a `fine` ledger row of minutes_late x rate is written immediately and the teacher is notified of the deduction. The subscribed students are also notified that the teacher has joined.
IDEMPOTENT: repeat calls the same day do not re-record, re-fine or re-notify.

There is intentionally no separate teacher check-in endpoint - this is it.

request.description:
**Last changed in:** update-10  |  **Auth:** teacher token

**What changed, update by update:**
- **update-2** - companion to the existing single-slot POST /teacher/consultations.
- **update-6** - accepts an optional `meeting_link`, written to every slot the run creates (migration 107).
- **update-10** - CHANGED: create consultation slots - now from a list of dates, and with an optional hourly price

---

update-10 (NEW FIELD `dates`): the days can now be an explicit list instead of a weekly pattern.

`dates` takes an array of `YYYY-MM-DD` strings - the days somebody picked on a calendar. They need not share a weekday, need not repeat, and need no end date. When it is present, `days` and `end_date` are ignored.

The old form is untouched and still works exactly as it did: leave `dates` out, send `days` (weekday names) and `end_date`, and every repeat up to that date is created. It was the only form available, and it could only describe a run that falls on the same weekday every week - which most consultation timetables do not, because a week gets skipped for a holiday and two days get added before an exam.

Both forms are held to the same window: nothing before today, nothing more than 180 days ahead, at most 200 slots in one call. A date outside it is REFUSED by name rather than quietly dropped - an admin who picks twelve dates and is given nine has no way to tell which three went missing.

update-10 (NEW FIELD `price_per_hour`): optional, and blank is not zero. An empty value means the consultation is not priced, which is what every consultation on the platform was before this; a `0` means it is deliberately free. The two are stored and served apart. A negative or non-numeric value is refused. Needs migration 124; without it the field is accepted and ignored rather than failing.

---

update-2 (Teacher): companion to the existing single-slot POST /teacher/consultations. Instead of creating one dated slot, this materializes one consultation_slots row PER matching calendar date for every selected weekday between today and end_date (inclusive) — e.g. days=[Saturday,Thursday] with end_date next month creates one slot for every upcoming Saturday and every upcoming Thursday up to that date, all at the same slot_time. Safety caps: end_date cannot be more than 180 days out, and a single call cannot generate more than 200 dates total (split into multiple calls if needed). Any date that would collide with an existing (teacher_id, slot_time, slot_date) slot is silently skipped, not duplicated or erroring the whole request — the response reports how many were created vs skipped. Exactly ONE notification is sent for the whole batch (not one per generated slot).

update-6 (CHANGED): accepts an optional `meeting_link`, written to every slot the run creates (migration 107).

update-10 (NEW FIELDS on every consultation slot): `price_per_hour` (a number, or null when nobody has priced it) and `is_free` (true only when a price was set and it is zero). Reading a missing price as 0 would show every slot created before update-10 as a giveaway, which is why the two are separate fields.

update-3 (NEW, Section 10). The teacher's way to avoid being fined for a class they already know they will miss or be late to. The request always goes to the ADMIN for review (PUT /admin/attendance/exceptions) - never to another teacher.

WHY IT MATTERS: once approved, that occurrence is marked `is_excused = 1`, which (a) suppresses the automatic fine and (b) keeps it out of the monthly unauthorized-absence counter that would otherwise eventually set `is_attendance_suspended = 1`. A rejected or never-filed request means the normal automatic consequences apply.

VALIDATION, in the order the server checks it:
1. session_id > 0 and a parseable occurrence_date, else `session_id_and_date_required`.
2. request_type must be exactly 'absence_permission' or 'late_notice', else `request_type_required`.
3. reason must be non-empty, else `reason_required`.
4. for 'late_notice', expected_minutes_late must be present and > 0, else `expected_minutes_late_required`.
5. the session must exist AND belong to this teacher, else `session_not_found_or_not_owned`.
6. there must be no OTHER still-pending request from this same teacher for this same (session_id, occurrence_date), else `request_already_pending`. Note this only blocks duplicates while one is pending - after a rejection the teacher may file again.

update-1: response now also includes is_subscribed on the student object (same computation as the one already returned by the profile endpoint: true if the student has at least one accessible course via get_student_accessible_entities()).

=== update-4 (BREAKING FOR CLIENTS): DEVICE LIMIT ===

An account may only be signed in from a limited number of devices - one by default. One set of credentials shared around a class was the cheapest way to give a paid course away, and nothing noticed it before.

CLIENT ACTION, REQUIRED: send a `device_id` with every login (body field, or the `X-Device-Id` header). It must be an id the client generates ONCE and keeps - a random uuid in localStorage is enough. Do NOT generate a fresh one per login: the server counts devices, so a new id every time burns through the student's slots immediately. Optional `device_name` and `platform` are what an admin sees in the devices list, so send something human.

While the limit is enabled, a login with NO device id is REFUSED with `error_code: device_id_required`. Letting an unidentified client through would make the whole limit decorative - anyone could drop the field for unlimited sessions.

TWO NEW REFUSALS, both HTTP 200 with `status: "error"` and an `error_code` to branch on:
- `device_id_required` - the client sent no device id.
- `device_limit_reached` - the account is already at its ceiling. The response also carries `max_devices` and `active_devices`. This is NOT a wrong-password error and must not be shown as one: the message tells the student to contact support, because only an admin can free a slot (POST /admin/students/devices/reset).

A device that has signed in before reuses its own slot, so signing in again from the same browser is always allowed.

ON EVERY LATER REQUEST: the access token now carries the device id, and the student auth middleware re-checks that the device is still authorised. A revoked device gets HTTP 401 with `error_code: device_revoked` - treat that as a hard logout, not as a refresh-the-token signal. POST /auth/refresh is gated the same way and answers 403 with the same code, so a revoked device cannot mint itself fresh tokens.

Tokens issued BEFORE this change carry no device id and are left alone, so turning the limit on does not sign out everyone already logged in.

A parent viewing their child (POST /parent/auth/login-as-student) mints a student token with no device id: it does not consume one of the child's slots and is never blocked by the child's limit.

TURNING IT OFF: set `site_settings.student_device_limit_enabled` to `0`. Devices are still recorded, but nothing is refused - use this if a client that cannot be updated yet has to keep working.

update-4 (CHANGED): subject to the login limit when `login_lockout_enabled` is on (migration 074). After `max_login_attempts` failures the response is `error_code: login_locked` with `retry_after_minutes`, and the CORRECT password is refused too until the lock expires. Counted per (email + IP + role), so an attacker can only ever lock out their own address - not the account holder's. The lock expires on its own; an admin can release every lock with POST /admin/login-attempts/clear. Ships OFF.

update-4 (CHANGED): THE EMAIL VERIFICATION GATE IS GONE FOR STUDENTS. Sign-up no longer sends a code and the email itself is optional, so `is_email_verified = 0` is an ordinary state rather than a blocked one - every account created before this change sits at 0, and refusing those would have locked out exactly the students removing verification was meant to let in. The response therefore never returns `requires_email_verification` for a student. Teachers, parents and admins keep their own gates; this is a student-only change.

**What changed, update by update:**

update-4 (CHANGED): refused with `error_code: registration_disabled` while the `registration_enabled` setting is 0 (migration 074).

Checked before anything is read or written, so a closed platform never half-creates an account and never sends a verification email for one that will not exist. Existing accounts are unaffected - only new sign-ups are closed. The message shown is the admin-editable `registration_disabled_message_ar` / `_en`.

Teacher registration is deliberately NOT covered: a teacher account does not work until an admin approves it, so it is already gated by a person.

update-4 (CHANGED): THE EMAIL IS OPTIONAL. `students.email` was NOT NULL with a UNIQUE key, which is why the form could not simply stop requiring it - an empty string would have been stored and the second student without an email would have collided with the first. Migration 095 makes the column nullable, because MySQL allows any number of NULLs in a UNIQUE index. Required now: `name` and `password`, plus EITHER an email OR a phone number - an account with neither would be created and immediately unreachable, so that case is refused with `error_code: email_or_phone_required`. `academic_year_id` and `study_language` were already optional in the handler; only the form was demanding them.

update-4 (CHANGED): NO VERIFICATION CODE. Nothing is generated and nothing is sent. The row is written with `is_email_verified = 1` - not left at 0 - so that screens still reading the column do not show a permanent "unverified" badge against an account nobody will ever be asked to verify. The response no longer carries a `verification` object; it carries `requires_email_verification: false` (always) and the usual `tokens`, so the student is signed in by the act of signing up.

update-4 (CHANGED): `default_phone_dial_code` in site_settings is seeded to 961 (Lebanon) by migration 095. The setting already existed and had never been given a value, so the hard-coded fallback behind it - Egypt's 20 - was what a number typed without a country code became.

=== update-7 ===

The account's picture can now be set AT SIGN-UP, in `image`, exactly as `PUT /user/student/auth/profile` already accepted it: a `data:image/...;base64,` payload, a multipart file, or a path that has already been uploaded. `avatar`, `photo`, `profile_image`, `picture` and `file` are accepted as aliases, in the body or as the multipart field name.

The field was technically read before this, but stored verbatim - an app sending a picture the way every other screen sends one wrote a whole base64 payload into a column that holds a filename, so the picture only appeared once the profile screen had been opened a second time to set it again. A caller that was already sending an uploaded path is unaffected: such a value still passes through unchanged.

Still optional. An account with no picture is normal, and one can be added later from the profile screen.

---

update-4 (NEW). Returns the resolved `country`, the `currency` prices will be quoted in, the `base_currency` everything falls back to, and `source`.

RESOLUTION ORDER, most authoritative first: `client` (an explicit `?country=` or `X-Country`), `student` (the country on the student's own record), `edge` (a CF-IPCountry / X-Vercel-IP-Country header the CDN already filled in), `geoip` (a cached lookup of the address), `base` (nothing resolved - the base currency).

`source` exists for support. When a student says "it is showing me dollars", the first thing anyone needs to know is whether that came from their profile, their address, or from falling all the way through - and there is no other way to tell.

The token is optional and changes the answer: a signed-in student who has chosen a country gets `student`.

---

update-15 (CHANGED): WHERE THE REQUEST COMES FROM now decides the price.

The country saved on the student used to sit second and beat both live signals, so a student connecting from Germany kept being quoted the base price - `source` came back as `student` and nothing about the connection could outrank it.

`students.country_id` cannot carry that weight. It holds three things that are indistinguishable once written - what registration captured, what the student later chose, and what an earlier geo-IP lookup wrote into it - so "the student told us where they live" was often not true.

The order is now: an explicit `country=` (the switcher) → the CDN header → a geo-IP lookup → the saved country → the base currency. The saved country remains the fallback for when there is no header and the lookup fails or is circuit-broken, which still beats the base currency.

The lookup's answer is also no longer written back into `students.country_id`. That stamp turned one connection into a permanent verdict and destroyed the NULL that means "detect it each time", so a stamped student could never return to automatic. Where someone connects from is read per request; where they LIVE is theirs to state, through POST /student/pricing/country.

Trade-off, stated plainly: a student travelling or on a VPN is priced where they are rather than where they live. That was already true of every signed-out visitor, so the old rule only protected signed-in purchases and only half the time.

Not equality - EasyKash ADDS ITS FEE ON TOP of what was requested (ask it for 2.00 and it reports 3.00), so an equality check would have rejected every genuine payment. A short payment is refused and both figures are logged. If no amount field arrives at all, that is recorded as "not verified" rather than treated as a match.

The grant is claimed atomically, so this and the student's own confirm cannot both grant the same purchase.

A refund reported here withdraws access: it closes the one subscription that payment opened - matched by grant reference and student, not by course - and cancels the affiliate commission only while it is still pending. A commission already paid out is left alone.
